extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in geometric analysis / Ricci flow
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition and proofs of maximum/principle-type results and Li-Yau(-Hamilton)/Perelman estimates for the Ricci flow and related parabolic PDEs; includes lemmas used to reduce PDE statements to ODE/fiberwise statements and various Harnack/pinch estimates. Targeted at deriving and applying comparison/monotonicity inequalities in geometric flows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hamilton’s advanced maximum principle (Theorem 2.3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let K be a closed subset of V satisfying the hypothesis (H1) and (H2). Suppose that for any x ∈ M and any solution σ_x(t) of the ODE dσ_x/dt = N(x,σ_x,t) which starts in K_x at t0 will remain in K_x for all later times. Then for any initial time t0 ∈ [0,T) the solution σ(x,t) of the PDE will remain in K for all later times provided σ(x,t) starts in K at time t0 and σ(x,t) is uniformly bounded with respect to the bundle metric h_ab on M and any initial time t0 ∈ [t0,T].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a fiberwise comparison principle: to show a PDE section stays in a closed convex subset K of a vector bundle, check (i) K is closed (and satisfies bundle invariance hypotheses (H1),(H2)), (ii) each fiber K_x is preserved by the corresponding ODE dσ_x/dt = N(x,·,t), and (iii) the PDE-solution is uniformly bounded (so one can restrict to a tubular neighborhood). The theorem reduces preservation under the PDE to preservation under the ODE in each fiber.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differential inequality lemma for Lipschitz functions (Lemma 2.3.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose ϕ : [a,b] → R is Lipschitz continuous and suppose for some constant C < +∞ we have dϕ/dt (in the sense of limsup of forward difference quotients) ≤ Cϕ(t) whenever ϕ(t) ≥ 0 on [a,b). If ϕ(a) ≤ 0 then ϕ(t) ≤ 0 on [a,b].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard Gronwall-type trick: replace ϕ by e^{−Ct}ϕ to reduce to C=0, then use the forward-limsup derivative property to deduce nonpositivity. The lemma is used to conclude a sup/distance function starting at zero stays zero.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivative estimate for a sup-function (Lemma 2.3.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let X be a complete smooth manifold and Y ⊂ X compact. Let ψ(x,t) be smooth on X×[a,b] and define ϕ(t)=sup_{y∈Y} ψ(y,t). Then ϕ is Lipschitz and dϕ/dt ≤ sup_{y∈Y, ψ(y,t)=ϕ(t)} ∂ψ/∂t (y,t).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This bridges pointwise ODE information to the evolution of a global sup/distance function. The proof uses compactness of Y and the mean value theorem on sequences achieving the sup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of ODE preservation of closed convex sets in R^n (Lemma 2.3.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let U ⊂ R^n open and Z ⊂ U a closed convex subset. For ODE dϕ/dt = N(ϕ,t) with N continuous and Lipschitz in ϕ, the following are equivalent: (i) any solution starting in Z at t0 remains in Z for later times; (ii) for every ϕ ∈ ∂Z and t ∈ [0,T], ϕ + N(ϕ,t) ∈ T_ϕ Z (equivalently l(N(ϕ,t)) ≤ 0 for every support linear functional l at ϕ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a tangent-cone/support-function criterion to check ODE invariance of convex sets. The proof uses support functions, the distance function s(ϕ)=dist(ϕ,Z) and Lemma 2.3.3 together with a cutoff argument to reduce to compact Z.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method: reduce PDE preservation to fiberwise ODE via sup/distance function
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct s(t)=sup_{x,η,l} [ l(σ(x,t)−η) − ε e^{At} f(x) ] where η ranges over closest points in ∂K_x and l over unit support functionals; use Lemma 2.3.3 to estimate ds/dt, Lemma 2.3.4 to control ODE terms, and Lemma 2.3.2 to conclude s(t) ≤ 0 hence σ(x,t) stays in K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key technical ingredients: choose a global cutoff f with bounded derivatives, insert an arbitrarily small perturbation ε e^{At} f(x) to localize and gain strict inequalities, estimate Laplacian and covariant derivative terms by extending η and l by parallel translation, and apply the three lemmas in combination. This is the blueprint used in the proof of Theorem 2.3.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chow–Lu time-dependent generalization (Theorem 2.3.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let K(t) ⊂ V, t ∈ [0,T] be closed subsets satisfying (H3) invariance under parallel translation by ∇^t, (H4) each fiber K_x(t) nonempty, closed and convex for each t, and (H5) the space-time track ∪_t (∂K(t) × {t}) is closed in V×[0,T]. Suppose for any x and any solution σ_x(t) of the ODE which starts in K_x(t0) the solution remains in K_x(t) for later times. Then any uniformly bounded solution σ(x,t) of the PDE that starts in K(t0) at t0 remains in K(t) for later times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This extends Theorem 2.3.1 to time-dependent constraint sets K(t); the same fiberwise-to-PDE reduction applies but one must ensure space-time closedness and parallel-translation invariance at each time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hamilton–Ivey curvature pinching estimate (Theorem 2.4.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose we have a solution to the Ricci flow on a three-manifold which is complete with bounded curvature for each t ≥ 0. Let λ ≥ µ ≥ ν be the eigenvalues of the curvature operator and R = λ+µ+ν. Assume at t=0 the eigenvalues are bounded below (text uses a lower bound ν ≥ −1 as normalization). Then at all points and times t ≥ 0 the pinching estimate holds: R ≥ (−ν)[ log(−ν) − 3 ] whenever ν < 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof constructs an O(3)-invariant closed convex set K in the 3×3 curvature-operator space defined by inequalities involving R and a concave inverse f^{-1}, checks K is preserved by the ODE system for eigenvalues dλ/dt = λ^2 + µν etc., and then applies Theorem 2.3.1 to deduce preservation under the Ricci flow. The estimate gives control of the most negative sectional curvature compared to the positive curvature as curvature blows up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion: construct O(3)-invariant closed convex sets in curvature operator space
rubrics_metrics.description: Any closed convex subset of the curvature-operator space that is invariant under the O(3)-action and preserved by the corresponding ODE for the curvature operator will be preserved under the Ricci flow (by Theorem 2.3.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the mechanism used to produce pinching estimates: define K by inequalities (some linear, some involving concave/convex functions of trace or eigenvalues), verify convexity and ODE-preservation, then apply the advanced maximum principle to the PDE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Li–Yau gradient estimate for the heat equation (Theorem 2.5.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let (M,g) be a complete n-dimensional Riemannian manifold with nonnegative Ricci curvature. Let u(x,t)>0 solve ∂u/∂t = ∆u on M×(0,∞). Then (2.5.1) holds: ∂u/∂t − 2|∇u|^2/u + (n/2t) u ≥ 0 (equivalently a standard Li–Yau inequality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is also a vector-field version (2.5.2): for any vector field V^i, ∂u/∂t + 2∇_i u V^i + u|V|^2 + (n/2t)u ≥ 0; picking the optimal V = −∇u/u recovers (2.5.1). Li–Yau is proved by considering the heat-kernel/soliton equality case and then maximum-principle arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Li–Yau estimate for scalar curvature on surfaces (Theorem 2.5.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let g_{ij}(x,t) be a complete solution of the Ricci flow on a surface with initial scalar curvature bounded, nonnegative everywhere and positive somewhere. Then the scalar curvature R(x,t) satisfies (2.5.4): ∂R/∂t − 2|∇R|^2/R + R/t ≥ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set L = log R and consider Q = ∂L/∂t − |∇L|^2 + 1/t; compute an evolution inequality for Q and apply the maximum principle (using a local version / cutoff if noncompact). This yields a differential Harnack inequality and then a path-integral Harnack.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harnack inequality for scalar curvature on surfaces (Corollary 2.5.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a complete Ricci-flow solution on a surface with bounded nonnegative scalar curvature, and 0 < t1 < t2 and x1,x2 ∈ M, one has R(x2,t2) ≥ exp(− d_{t1}(x1,x2)^2 / (4(t2−t1))) · (t1/t2) · R(x1,t1) (path-integral form derived from the Li–Yau estimate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pick a geodesic path γ(τ) with constant speed from x1 at t1 to x2 at t2, integrate the Li–Yau inequality along the space-time path and optimize to obtain the exponential term involving the squared distance divided by time difference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Li–Yau–Hamilton matrix estimate (Theorem 2.5.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let g_{ij}(x,t) be a complete solution with bounded curvature to the Ricci flow on M for t ∈ (0,T) and suppose the curvature operator is nonnegative. Then for any one-form W_a and any two-form U_{ab} one has Mab W^a W^b + 2 P_{abc} U^{ab} W^c + R_{abcd} U^{ab} U^{cd} ≥ 0 on M×(0,T), where Mab = ∆R_{ab} - (1/2)∇_a∇_b R + ... and P_{abc} = ∇_a R_{bc} - ∇_b R_{ac}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This matrix quadratic vanishes on expanding solitons and its nonnegativity is established by computing its evolution ∂/∂t − ∆ and applying a maximum principle argument after arranging suitable extensions of W,U so first derivatives vanish at a minimizing point; decomposition into sums of squares yields positivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trace/one-form corollary (Corollary 2.5.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any one-form V^a, ∂R/∂t + R/t + 2 ∇_a R V^a + 2 R_{ab} V^a V^b ≥ 0. In particular tR(x,t) is pointwise nondecreasing in time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the scalar trace version of the Li–Yau–Hamilton matrix estimate. Setting V≡0 gives monotonicity of tR; combining monotonicity with local derivative estimates yields elliptic-type control of curvature derivatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local derivative (elliptic-type) estimate from Li–Yau–Hamilton (Corollary 2.5.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose a Ricci flow solution for t>0 is complete with bounded curvature and nonnegative curvature operator, and at some time t we have R ≤ M on the geodesic ball B(p,r). Then for k=1,2,... the k-th order derivatives of curvature at p at time t satisfy a bound of the form |∇^k Rm(p,t)| ≤ C_k M^2 (1/r^{2k} + 1/t^k + M^k) (C_k depends on dimension and k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use monotonicity of tR to obtain a uniform bound for earlier times and then apply Shi-type local derivative estimates combined with shrinking metric property under nonnegative curvature operator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Higher-dimensional Harnack inequality (Corollary 2.5.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let g_{ij}(x,t) be a complete Ricci-flow solution with bounded and nonnegative curvature operator. For x1,x2 ∈ M and 0 < t1 < t2, one has an inequality of Harnack type: R(x2,t2) ≥ exp(− d_{t1}(x1,x2)^2 / (2(t2−t1)) ) · (t1/t2) · R(x1,t1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous to the two-dimensional case but with constants adapted to the matrix Li–Yau–Hamilton estimate; obtained by integrating the trace inequality along space-time paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kähler-Ricci Li–Yau–Hamilton estimate (Theorem 2.5.9 and Corollary 2.5.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a complete solution g_{α arβ}(x,t) to the Kähler-Ricci flow with bounded curvature and nonnegative holomorphic bisectional curvature, define Q_{α arβ} = ∂/∂t R_{α arβ} + R_{α arγ} R_{γ arβ} + ∇_γ R_{α arβ} V^γ + ∇_{ arγ} R_{α arβ} V^{ arγ} + (1/t) R_{α arβ}. Then Q_{α arβ} W^α W^{ arβ} ≥ 0 for all V,W and t>0. Consequently (i) the scalar curvature satisfies ∂R/∂t − 2|∇R|^2/R + R/t ≥ 0, and (ii) if R_{α arβ}>0 then φ = det(R_{α arβ})/det(g_{α arβ}) satisfies ∂φ/∂t − 2|∇φ|^2/φ + (nφ)/t ≥ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Kähler setting weakens curvature hypotheses (nonnegative bisectional curvature) but gives matrix and determinant-level Harnack-type inequalities; proofs follow the same Li–Yau–Hamilton template adapted to complex indices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perelman’s Li–Yau-type estimate for conjugate heat equation (Lemma 2.6.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let g_{ij}(x,t) be a complete Ricci-flow solution on [0,T) and let u = (4πτ)^{-n/2} e^{−f} be a solution of the conjugate heat equation ∂u/∂τ − ∆u + R u = 0 with τ = T − t. Define H = 2∆f − |∇f|^2 + R + f/τ − n/τ (text gives an equivalent combination) and v = τ H u. Then ∂H/∂τ = ∆H − 2∇f·∇H − (1/τ) H − 2 | R_{ij} + ∇_i ∇_j f − (1/2τ) g_{ij} |^2, and ∂v/∂τ = ∆v − R v − 2τ u | R_{ij} + ∇_i ∇_j f − (1/2τ) g_{ij} |^2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These evolution formulas show H (and v) satisfy parabolic inequalities with a negative definite square term, providing monotonicity/entropy-type information for conjugate heat kernels. The identities are obtained by writing the shrinking soliton identities and differentiating, then rewriting in terms of f and u and computing ∂/∂τ − ∆.
